digest.component_or_area: test harness / local development environment / detached suite validation
propositions: Detached pytest runs (via nohup) report errors that do not reproduce in foreground shells, attributed to innocent tests when the real cause is external checkout mutation concurrent with the suite.

The _no_repo_root_leaks autouse fixture cannot distinguish between in-test mutations and concurrent external writes to REPO_ROOT, causing false-positive error attribution and silent deletion of concurrent agent files.

Child processes killed by signal (e.g., SIGKILL on a signal-killed browser probe) report empty stderr, and the e2e conftest diagnostic raises on empty stdout without inspecting proc.returncode, making signal-death indistinguishable from real product regression.

Detachment itself does not cause the failure; detachment is only the enabler because it allows concurrent external actors to mutate the checkout while the suite runs, whereas a foreground run blocks the agent from doing so.

The leak-guard message falsely asserts 'Test leaked new entries into REPO_ROOT' when the entry may come from a concurrent process outside the test, eroding signal by misattributing external mutations to innocent tests.

Documentation for validating the whole test tree locally via detached runs (with guidance on dedicated worktrees and mutual exclusion) does not exist; detached-suite practice is entirely undocumented folklore.
